title: Microsoft Purview: per-policy coverage report for auto-labeling
summary: Hold: the path to the policy review pages omits the documented Solutions step, and the briefing asserts coverage-report permissions that Microsoft documents only for other review pages. The roadmap dates, coverage-report prerequisites, 30-day window and PowerShell command are supported, but categorical assurances about read-only behaviour and end-user impact need narrowing.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview Information Protection adds an auto-labeling per-policy coverage report.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Information Protection-Auto-labeling per-policy coverage report

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The report compares policy enforcement with the latest simulation run.
claims.quote: For each enforced auto-labeling policy, admins can view how files processed during enforcement correlate to the latest simulation run.

claims.claim: The report shows labeled and not-yet-labeled file volumes and their relationship to the simulation snapshot.
claims.quote: The per-policy coverage report shows volumes of files that have been labeled or are not yet labeled, and whether those files were included in the last simulation snapshot.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The report is strictly read-only and applies no labels itself.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling per-policy coverage report read-only no labels end users. Read MC1456609, apply-sensitivity-label-automatically (coverage and monitoring), and troubleshooting search excerpts; they describe reporting, not an explicit read-only guarantee.
claims.fix: Replace 'Read-only', 'The report only reads; it applies no labels itself' and the read-only premise in the risk rationale with 'Microsoft describes the report as monitoring auto-labeling enforcement outcomes.' Keep the separate advice about simulation matches.

claims.claim: Nothing changes for end users and end users notice nothing.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling per-policy coverage report read-only no labels end users. Read MC1456609 and the Learn monitoring and coverage sections; Microsoft identifies administrators as affected but does not state that no end user can notice any change.
claims.fix: Remove 'and nothing in the tenant changes for end users' from Why it matters and 'end users notice nothing' from the impact rationale. Retain the documented administrator audience.

claims.quote: Identify files that remain pending, have not yet been processed, or are no longer eligible for labeling because they were deleted or modified after the simulation run.- Investigate files where label application was unsuccessful.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The policy review pages require Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator, Information Protection Admin or Information Protection Analyst.
claims.quote:
To view the review pages, you need one of the following roles:

- Compliance Administrator
- Compliance Data Administrator
- Information Protection Admin
- Information Protection Analyst

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Access to the coverage report follows the four roles documented for the per-policy review pages.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview "coverage by simulation context" "role"; "View coverage" permissions roles enable disable license pricing. Read the cited Learn coverage and policy-review sections and Purview permissions excerpts; no passage extends those review-page roles explicitly to coverage.
claims.fix: Replace both assertions that coverage access follows the review-page roles with 'Learn lists these roles for the per-policy review pages but does not separately state the permissions required for View coverage.' In Governance controls, qualify the content-preview statement as applying to matched content in the review pages, not an established coverage-report preview.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Viewing matched text or file contents in the documented review experience also requires Data Classification Content Viewer.
claims.quote: **Contextual summary** is available in supported portal experiences. To view matched text inside a file, you also need the **Data Classification Content Viewer** role.

claims.claim: Global administrators do not have Data Classification Content Viewer by default.
claims.quote: Viewing file contents in the source view requires the **Data Classification Content Viewer** role (included in the Content Explorer Content Viewer, Information Protection, and Information Protection Investigators role groups). Global admins don't have this role by default.

claims.claim: Turning a policy on after simulation requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.
claims.quote: Turning a policy from **Ready to turn on** to **On** requires **Compliance Administrator** or **Compliance Data Administrator**.

claims.quote: Auto-labeling isn't currently available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency.

claims.quote: If your tenant can't support this functionality, the **Auto-labeling** page isn't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.quote:
go to **Information Protection** > **Policies** > **Auto-labeling policies**.

claims.quote: Searched: "coverage" "AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy"; "auto-labeling" "coverage" "Graph". Opened Learn apply-sensitivity-label-automatically and Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy; found labeling progress, not a simulation-context coverage-data interface.

claims.claim: Policy review pages open through Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details.
claims.quote: To open the newer review pages, go to **Solutions** > **Information Protection** > **Policies** > **Auto-labeling policies**. Select a policy, then select **View details** in the policy details panel.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path and its rendered-table path with 'Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details'. The cited page explicitly includes Solutions for this review-page route.

Opened Learn auto-labeling coverage and Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy; read MC1456609. Found eligibility conditions and navigation, not a separate report toggle.

Remove the standalone 'Run a simulation on any policy that has not had one, as Microsoft's notice recommends' checklist bullet and shorten the After rollout bullet to 'Review coverage within the 30 days after each simulation run.' Keep the supported simulation prerequisite and expiry explanation in the body.
